scope.heading: Topics
items: Treaty of Versailles (aims of the leaders, Germany's punishments)

flashcards.back: The name for Germany's democratic government from 1919 to 1933. It is named after the town of Weimar, where its constitution was written.
A government where one person or one party has total power. People cannot vote them out.
A system where people vote to choose their government.
The Nazi secret police. They spied on people and arrested opponents without a trial.
The German emperor. Kaiser Wilhelm II gave up the throne in November 1918, at the end of the First World War.
The peace treaty between Germany and the Allies after the First World War. It was signed in June 1919.
The leaders who decided the treaty: Clemenceau (France), Lloyd George (Britain) and Woodrow Wilson (USA).
To punish Germany harshly and make sure it could never attack France again.
To punish Germany, but not too harshly, so Germany could still trade with Britain and would not want revenge.
A fair peace based on his Fourteen Points, and a League of Nations to keep peace.
Article 231 of the treaty. Germany had to accept the blame for starting the war.
Money Germany had to pay for war damage. In 1921 the amount was set at £6.6 billion.
Land, Army, Money and Blame.
Germany lost about 13% of its land, including Alsace-Lorraine to France, and all of its colonies.
Only 100,000 soldiers, no conscription, no tanks, no air force, no submarines and only 6 battleships. The Rhineland had to be demilitarised.
A dictated peace. Germans called the treaty a diktat because they were forced to sign it.
Part of the Weimar constitution. It let the President make laws in an emergency without the Reichstag.
The German parliament.
Parties got seats in the same proportion as their votes. This led to many small parties and weak coalition governments.
Prices rose so fast that money became worthless. The government printed more and more money after French and Belgian troops took over the Ruhr.
French and Belgian troops took over the Ruhr industrial area because Germany missed a reparations payment.
A communist revolt in Berlin. It was crushed by the Freikorps (ex-soldiers).
A Weimar leader who helped Germany recover. He brought in a new currency and the Dawes Plan (American loans) in 1924.
Hitler's failed attempt to take power by force in Munich. He was arrested and sent to prison.
'My Struggle'. The book Hitler wrote in prison after the Munich Putsch, setting out his ideas.

flashcards.front: What did Hitler learn from the Munich Putsch?
flashcards.back: That he should try to win power legally, through elections, not by force.
A world economic crisis that started with the Wall Street Crash in 1929. By 1932 about 6 million Germans were unemployed.
Hitler was appointed Chancellor of Germany.
The parliament building burned down. Hitler blamed the communists and used it to arrest opponents.
A law that let Hitler make laws without the Reichstag. It gave him the power of a dictator.
Hitler had Ernst Röhm, the leader of the SA, and other rivals killed.
'Leader'. Hitler's title from August 1934, when he combined the jobs of Chancellor and President.
Hitler's elite guard, led by Heinrich Himmler. It ran the police and the concentration camps.
Information used to control what people think. Joseph Goebbels was in charge of Nazi propaganda.
Controlling what people can read, hear and see. The Nazis banned books, newspapers and films they did not like.

quiz.q: When was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
quiz.explain: It was signed in June 1919 in the Palace of Versailles, near Paris.

quiz.q: Which leader wanted to punish Germany the most harshly?
quiz.explain: Clemenceau of France wanted revenge and security for France.

quiz.q: What was the War Guilt Clause?
options: Germany had to leave the League of Nations
Germany had to accept blame for the war
Germany had to pay for new roads
Germany had to choose a new Kaiser
quiz.explain: Article 231 made Germany accept the blame for starting the war.

quiz.q: How big could the German army be after the treaty?
quiz.explain: The army was limited to 100,000 soldiers, with no conscription.

quiz.q: What did Woodrow Wilson want?
options: A fair peace and a League of Nations
quiz.explain: Wilson's Fourteen Points aimed for a fair, lasting peace.

quiz.q: Which area did Germany lose to France?
quiz.explain: Alsace-Lorraine was returned to France.

quiz.q: What did Article 48 allow?
options: The President to make laws in an emergency
quiz.explain: Article 48 gave the President emergency powers.

quiz.q: In which year did hyperinflation hit Germany?
quiz.explain: In 1923 money became almost worthless.

quiz.q: Why did French and Belgian troops occupy the Ruhr in 1923?
quiz.explain: They took goods instead when Germany did not pay.

quiz.q: Why did proportional representation make Weimar governments weak?
options: Many small parties had to form coalitions
quiz.explain: Coalitions often disagreed and fell apart.

quiz.q: Who helped Germany recover after 1923?
quiz.explain: Stresemann brought in a new currency and the Dawes Plan.

quiz.q: Where did the 1923 Putsch take place?
quiz.explain: It started in a beer hall in Munich, Bavaria.

quiz.q: What happened to Hitler after the Munich Putsch?
options: He was put on trial and sent to prison
quiz.explain: He was sentenced to five years but served about nine months.

quiz.q: What book did Hitler write in prison?
quiz.explain: Mein Kampf means 'My Struggle'.

quiz.q: What event in 1929 led to the Great Depression?
quiz.explain: The Wall Street Crash in the USA caused a world economic crisis.

quiz.q: When did Hitler become Chancellor?
quiz.explain: President Hindenburg appointed him on 30 January 1933.

quiz.q: What did the Enabling Act do?
options: Let Hitler make laws without the Reichstag
quiz.explain: It gave Hitler the power of a dictator.

quiz.q: Who was killed on the Night of the Long Knives?
quiz.explain: Hitler removed Röhm, the SA leader, and others in June 1934.

quiz.q: What was the Gestapo?
quiz.explain: The Gestapo spied on people and arrested opponents.

quiz.q: Who ran Nazi propaganda?
quiz.explain: Joseph Goebbels controlled the radio, films, newspapers and rallies.

quiz.q: Who did Hitler blame for the Reichstag Fire?
quiz.explain: He used it as an excuse to arrest communists.

bigger_picture.intro: These are the five questions on page 14 of your booklet. Read the paragraph on page 14 first. Stalin and Mussolini are background only. They are not the main test topics.

questions.q: What role did the Treaty of Versailles play in the rise of dictatorships in Europe?
questions.a: Its harsh terms made many Germans angry and humiliated. Extremist leaders like Hitler used this anger to win support.

questions.q: How did the Great Depression contribute to the rise of extremist movements?
questions.a: It caused mass unemployment and poverty. Desperate people turned to extreme parties that promised to fix things.

questions.q: Why did many people support authoritarian leaders in post-World War I Europe?
questions.a: Democratic governments seemed weak. People wanted strong leaders who promised order, jobs and national pride.

questions.q: How did Mussolini and Hitler exploit fears of communism to gain support?
questions.a: They said they would protect the country from a communist revolution. This won support from business owners, the middle classes and the army.

questions.q: What methods did Stalin use to consolidate power in the Soviet Union?
questions.a: Purges of rivals, propaganda, and a command economy where the state controlled industry and farming.
